newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Volatility trades struck in FTSE index.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Volatility trades struck in FTSE index.

text.p: Relatively calm conditions in the UK stock market on Thursday enabled traders with a view on market volatility to implement volatility trades in the FTSE 100 index options and futures, dealers said.
One of the larger deals by early afternoon was from a seller of 800 October 3950 puts at 40p who also sold December futures at 3975.
If the deal was correctly hedged, the gains from the short futures position as the market falls will be offset by losses from the short options position and vice versa if the market rises.
Profits will arise if market volatility decreases up to the October options expiry.
One trader with an opposite view, expecting volatility to increase over the coming months, bought 550 December 3900 puts at 65p against buying December futures at 3966.
By 1232 GMT, the cash index was down 8.5 at 3927.2 while December futures were down 4.0 at 3969.0.
Over in stock options one of the main deals was in supermarket chain Asda Group from a buyer of 1,000 January 100 calls at 9-1/2p.
Asda shares shed a penny to 104-1/2p.
In pharmaceuticals group Glaxo Wellcome a short strangle was the main deal and it involved the sale of 200 October 900 puts at 1/2p as well as 200 October 1000 calls at 5-1/2p.
The deal will make a maximum 6p profit at expiry if the underlying shares stay between 900p and 1000p when both options will be worthless.
